write_style.name: 网文
write_style.when: Use this register for fights, chases, confrontations, payoffs, plot turns, and any beat that has to move fast.
write_style.rhythm: 1. Use the beat of a popular web novel (爽文): little setup, hit the conflict fast, give the result fast, and keep the situation moving from paragraph to paragraph. 2. Do not write long lyrical passages, philosophical monologue, scenery used as an emotional proxy, complex metaphor, or slow-paced psychological build-up. 3. Action is emotion. 4. Every line of dialogue carries a hook. 5. Plant foreshadowing, land the payoffs, keep it satisfying. 6. Give the characters vitality; avoid flat, expository dialogue. 7. Reduce runs of "name/pronoun + action"; carry the action through a change of events, feedback from the environment, or an entry into dialogue. 8. Negative model: 龙族 (Dragon Raja). 9. Positive model: 斗破苍穹 (Battle Through the Heavens). 10. Do not imitate the 龙族 register; stay with fast, accessible 小白爽文 — push the plot hard, no fine-grained description.
write_style.diction: 1. Use natural spoken language, light internet slang, and in-character snark to make it feel real. 2. Sentences do not pile up ornate words, but they must render the scene fully. 3. It should be a satisfying read; do not tie emotions in knots. 4. Drive the plot with big action and dialogue while keeping a sense of rhythm in the sentences. 5. Describe from the user's subjective point of view: no subtext, no micro-action or facial-expression description, no explanation of manner, action, or speech, and skip everything outside the character's subjective perception.
write_style.dialogue: 1. Dialogue conveys tone, attitude, and emotion through its content alone. 2. Never describe voice, tone, manner of speech, timbre, pitch, volume, or emotional colour. 3. Never append "sound effect", "tone note", "emotional explanation", or "aura description" after a line of dialogue. 4. Once a character finishes speaking, go straight to the reaction, the action, the change in the situation, or the next line.
write_style.narration: 1. Narration stays in the present at all times: write only the image, the action, and the dialogue happening now. 2. Keep web-novel directness: clean scene transitions, flowing rhythm. 3. Do not use enumerating rhetoric and do not count things; render quantity with vague phrasing or a natural substitute word. 4. Once a character finishes an action or a line, go straight to the next image; add no motive, meaning, evaluation, or interpretation. 5. Avoid micro-action description: no fine-grained expression, gaze, finger, or breath detail that advances nothing. 6. Do not insert memory, summary, or psychological reading into action or dialogue. 7. Do not restate earlier information, and do not let a character repeat what someone else has already said. 8. Prefer short, forceful sentences; let character action drive the plot.
